title: The housekeeper
description: A young Vietnamese woman with short curled hair, in a pale embroidered blouse and dark skirt, stands laughing inside the camp wire with a small blue-grey camera in her hands, its strap looped on her wrist. Behind her a sandbagged emplacement, a double fence of barbed wire, prefabricated buildings under construction, and tin roofs and hills beyond. She is the housekeeper Larry says reached America: "She had 9 kids. Her and her mother would clean the hooch." Two days earlier: "She is the housekeeper who made it to america. The same one in front of T-122. This is in Tah Suhn Nhut."
researchNotes: Two comments, 2026-09-03 (giscus-vn-0151-c18260227.json) and 2026-09-05 (giscus-vn-0151-c18307708.json). Her name is not given. The survey had placed this frame at Nha Trang from the construction in the background; Larry's placement at the base is his and is entered, with the survey's reading left as a machine hypothesis. She holds a camera; whose it was is not on record. How the archive treats her (a private individual who may be living, or have living family) is ledger #26, issue #94, and is not discussed in this record.
